answer: We define the security of the protocol via a dynamic opportunity-cost bond registered on a randomness beacon. By modeling identity multiplication as a sequential game, the subgame-perfect slashing matrix forces adversarial deviation to cross a negative-utility ridge where the marginal cost of staking dominates any reward. Consequently, the utility space behaves like a flat meadow of zero exploitability, proving that the unique Nash equilibrium converges to honest participation, as the expected payoff of Sybil generation remains strictly negative.
